info.name: EDI Middleware — SAP B1 Integration
info.description:
Everything SAP Business One calls on the Let's Try Foods EDI middleware, and nothing else.

START HERE
1. Set the `baseUrl` and `email` / `password` collection variables.
2. Run '01 · Auth → Login' — every other request reuses the token it saves.

ONE ENDPOINT FOR ADD AND UPDATE
Every push endpoint decides for itself whether a record is new. You never have to ask first and you never get a 409 for sending something twice.

  materials           item_code                          -> ItemCode
  partners            code                               -> CardCode
  ship-to/sync        partner_code + buyer_whs_code      -> CardCode + Address
  bill-to/sync        partner_code + buyer_bill_to_code  -> CardCode + Address
  sku-mappings/sync   partner_code + buyer_sku           -> CardCode + item
  branches            bpl_id                             -> OBPL.BPLId
  warehouses          whs_code                           -> OWHS.WhsCode
  invoices            b1_invoice_doc_entry, then invoice_number -> DocEntry

Single-record endpoints answer 201 when they created and 200 when they updated. Batch (/sync) endpoints answer 200 and report created/updated/skipped counts — always read `errors[]`, a 200 does not mean every row was accepted.

TWO KEYS WORTH NOTING
SKU mappings key on `buyer_sku`, not `b1_item_code`: a customer can list one item under several of their own codes, and keying on the item would make the second push overwrite the first. `b1_item_code` is still required and must already exist in Item Master.

Warehouses need their branch first: `bpl_id` must already name a branch we hold, or the push is refused. A warehouse whose branch is unknown cannot decide place of supply.

Invoices match on `DocEntry` first because it is your immutable key; `invoice_number` is the fallback, since the first push usually has no DocEntry yet.

WHAT AN UPDATE WILL NOT OVERWRITE
Customer integration config (source_channel, gmail_label, webhook_secret, asn_sla_hours) — it describes how we fetch that retailer's orders, which a Business Partner record cannot express. Ops mappings (b1_whs_code, b1_bill_to_code, mapping_status). Soft-deleted rows, which answer 409 rather than being resurrected.

Full contract: docs/sap-master-data-api.md and docs/sap-invoice-api.md.

item.name: 04 · Invoices (SAP → us)
item.description: SAP pushes A/R Invoices here; receiving one raises and dispatches its ASN.

request.description:
Single endpoint for add and update. Safe to send repeatedly.

HOW WE DECIDE IT IS THE SAME INVOICE
`b1_invoice_doc_entry` is tried first — it is your immutable key, so a re-push carrying it lands on the same row whatever else changed. Sending it on every push is recommended.

`invoice_number` is the fallback and stays unique. It matters because the first push of an invoice usually has no DocEntry yet (B1 assigns it on posting, the IRN later still), and the number is what the retailer reconciles against.

REFUSED, NOT APPLIED: a DocEntry we already hold arriving under a DIFFERENT invoice_number. B1 does not renumber a posted invoice, so that means a cancel-and-repost or a wrong DocEntry — and renaming a stored invoice would break the ASN the retailer already holds against the old number.

The common re-push is the IRN: push the invoice immediately (we store it and send the ASN), then push again once the IRP returns the IRN and we fill it in.

{{poNumber}} and {{buyerSku}} come from 'List POs' / 'Get PO detail'. Run those first, or hardcode real values.

ALWAYS read results[] — an invoice can be stored but HELD (asn_dispatched=false) with the reason in issues[].

batch_number takes a string here; see 'line split across two batches' for the multi-batch form.

exec: console.log('created=' + b.created + ' updated=' + b.updated + ' skipped=' + b.skipped);

item.name: Push invoice — line split across two batches

request.description:
A line filled from more than one batch. The retailer books stock against a batch and matches it at goods-in, so they need the split, not the total.

RULES
• Batch quantities must total the line's qty (34 + 16 = 50). Anything else is rejected: summing to less under-declares the shipment, summing to more declares stock that was never invoiced.
• batchNumber / batch_number and expiryDate / expiry_date are both accepted. A batch with no expiry inherits the line's expiry_date.
• The plain string form still works and means one batch for the whole quantity, so nothing already sending it has to change.

WHAT THE PARTNER RECEIVES
Two rows, not one nested field — Blinkit §12.3 types batch_number as a single string per item and Zepto's batchDetails is one object per itemDetails entry. The rows share every per-unit figure (unit_price, MRP, landing price) and divide only the quantity.

Needs a real Sales Order, like the request above: set b1_sales_order_doc_entry, or run 'List POs' first so {{poNumber}} is filled. Without one you get outcome=ERROR with 'No Sales Order found'.

exec: console.log('outcome', r.outcome, '| asn', r.asn_number, '| dispatched', r.asn_dispatched);

item.name: NEGATIVE — batch quantities do not total the line (expect 422)

request.description:
34 + 10 = 44 against a line of 50. Rejected before anything is stored.

Worth seeing fail: the ASN goes out as one row per batch, so a short split would tell the retailer less had shipped than was billed, and that is found at the dock rather than here.

Needs a real Sales Order, like the request above: set b1_sales_order_doc_entry, or run 'List POs' first so {{poNumber}} is filled. Without one you get outcome=ERROR with 'No Sales Order found'.

request.description:
Single endpoint for both. Existence is decided on `code` (= SAP `CardCode`).

• 201 — created
• 200 — updated
• 409 — the customer is soft-deleted here; restore it first
• 422 — `source_channel` is not one of API / WEBHOOK / EMAIL / PORTAL / MANUAL

WHAT AN UPDATE WILL NOT OVERWRITE
`source_channel`, `gmail_label`, `webhook_secret` and `asn_sla_hours` describe how we FETCH this retailer's orders. A SAP Business Partner record has nothing to say about that, so they are written when the customer is created and thereafter only where still empty.

This matters: `source_channel` defaults to MANUAL in this schema, so sending it on a refresh is indistinguishable from omitting it. Applying that would demote a live API customer to MANUAL and stop its PO polling with no error anywhere. It is ignored unless the field is genuinely unset.

Creating the customer does not make POs flow — ingestion also needs an adapter and a parser in our code for this code. The response `warnings` say what is missing.

item.name: Add or update item  → 201 create / 200 update

request.description:
Single endpoint for both. Existence is decided on `item_code` (= SAP `ItemCode`) alone: absent means create, present means update.

• 201 — created
• 200 — updated
• 409 — the item is soft-deleted here; restore it first, so an automated push cannot undo a deliberate removal.

Safe to send repeatedly. You never have to ask whether we already hold it.

For a batch, use 'Sync items' in this folder — same behaviour, many rows, reports created/updated/skipped counts.

The same `item_code` with two fields changed. Answers 200 and applies them — no 409, no duplicate row.

Run 'Add or update item' first.

item.name: 10 · Master Data — Branch Master (OBPL)
item.description: Our own branches, mirrored from SAP OBPL. Unlike ship-to/bill-to there is no mapping decision here — SAP owns every business field; only is_active and notes are ours. Under the India localization the branch is the GST registration point that decides CGST/SGST vs IGST on a B1 document.

request.description:
Single endpoint for both. Existence is decided on `bpl_id` (= SAP `OBPL.BPLId`).

• 201 — created
• 200 — updated
• 409 — the branch is soft-deleted here; restore it first

Takes the same object `/branches/sync` takes in its list, so the two cannot drift.

`disabled` is SAP's flag and is always applied — a branch you re-enable stops being treated as closed on the next push. `is_active` and `notes` are ours and are never touched, so a push cannot undo an ops decision to park a branch.

item.name: 11 · Master Data — Warehouse Master (OWHS)
item.description: Our own warehouses, mirrored from SAP OWHS. Every warehouse belongs to a branch (OWHS.BPLid), and B1 rejects a marketing document whose warehouse and branch disagree — so branches must be synced first and re-parenting is a SAP change, not a dashboard one.

item.name: Add or update warehouse  → 201 create / 200 update

request.description:
Single endpoint for both. Existence is decided on `whs_code` (= SAP `OWHS.WhsCode`), upper-cased on receipt.

• 201 — created
• 200 — updated
• 409 — `bpl_id` names a branch we do not hold, OR the warehouse is soft-deleted here

PUSH BRANCHES FIRST. A warehouse whose branch is unknown cannot decide place of supply, so it is refused rather than stored with a dangling link — otherwise the failure surfaces much later as a rejected Sales Order.

`is_active` and `notes` are ours and are never touched.

The same `whs_code` with the name changed. Answers 200 and applies it.

Run 'Add or update warehouse' first.
